walkthroughs.body_html:
Atmospheric Systems & Societies — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atmospheric Systems & Societies brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atmospheric Systems & Societies.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
options: About 50 percent.
100 percent (everything transfers).
About 10 percent.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.
Decomposition.

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Decomposition.
Photosynthesis.
Respiration.
